findings.claim: A ₹15 crore SEBI penalty on Mukesh Ambani no longer stands: the Securities Appellate Tribunal set it aside in December 2023 and the Supreme Court dismissed SEBI's appeal in November 2024. SEBI had imposed it in January 2021, holding him responsible as managing director for Reliance's November 2007 trades in Reliance Petroleum shares, which it called manipulative.

SEBI found Reliance Industries' November 2007 trades in Reliance Petroleum fraudulent, ordered ₹447.27 crore disgorged and in 2021 fined it ₹25 crore; the tribunal upheld the company penalty. In May 2026 the Supreme Court set aside the fraud finding and the disgorgement but upheld a breach of position-limit disclosure rules.

findings.entity: Mukesh Ambani and other Reliance promoters
findings.claim: A joint ₹25 crore SEBI penalty on Mukesh Ambani, Anil Ambani, other family members and promoter entities no longer stands: the tribunal set it aside in July 2023 and the Supreme Court dismissed SEBI's appeal in November 2024. SEBI had imposed it in April 2021 for not making an open offer after a 2000 share acquisition, over 25 years ago.

findings.entity: Reliance Industries (KG-D6 consortium with BP and Niko)
findings.claim: India's government claims about US$1.55 billion from the Reliance-led KG-D6 consortium over gas it says migrated from neighbouring ONGC blocks. An arbitral tribunal rejected the claim in 2018, the Delhi High Court reversed that in February 2025, and in October 2026 the Supreme Court sent the pending appeals to mediation.

Election Commission data released in March 2024 showed Qwik Supply Chain was the third-largest electoral bond buyer: ₹410 crore in 2021-22 and 2023-24, about ₹385 crore of it to the BJP. Press reports link Qwik to Reliance through directors, addresses and shareholders; the link is disputed, and Reliance says Qwik is not a subsidiary of any Reliance entity.

The press-freedom NGO Reporters Without Borders, in its India profile for the 2026 index, characterises Mukesh Ambani as owning more than 70 media outlets followed by at least 800 million Indians and as a close friend of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This is the NGO's characterisation, not an official finding.

Reliance reports scope 1 and 2 emissions for its oil-to-chemicals and exploration businesses of 45.52 million tonnes CO2e in 2025-26, roughly flat since 2022-23 (45.24), with renewables about 1% of their energy use in 2024-25. It targets net carbon zero by 2035; the pages give no scope 3 figure.

Reliance Industries reports spending ₹2,156 crore on corporate social responsibility in 2024-25, across rural development, education, healthcare, women's empowerment, disaster management and other programmes.

ecology.reason: Oil refining and petrochemicals are Reliance's core business. Its own reports put scope 1 and 2 emissions of these businesses at about 45.5 million tonnes CO2e a year, roughly flat since 2022-23, with renewables about 1% of their energy use. It targets net carbon zero by 2035; no scope 3 figure is published on those pages.

politics.reason: The press-freedom NGO Reporters Without Borders says Mukesh Ambani owns more than 70 media outlets followed by at least 800 million Indians. Qwik Supply Chain, a firm press reports link to Reliance, was India's third-largest electoral bond buyer (₹410 crore, mostly to the BJP); the link is disputed, and Reliance says Qwik is not a subsidiary of any Reliance entity. No personal donation is documented.

legal.reason: No personal penalty stands. SEBI's two penalties naming Mukesh Ambani (₹15 crore over 2007 Reliance Petroleum trades, and a joint ₹25 crore with other promoters over a 2000 takeover) were set aside on appeal, and the Supreme Court dismissed SEBI's appeals in 2024. At company level, the Supreme Court in 2026 set aside SEBI's fraud finding and ₹447 crore disgorgement against Reliance but upheld a breach of position-limit disclosure rules.

unresolved.reason: The government's claim of about US$1.55 billion against the Reliance-led KG-D6 consortium over gas migration from ONGC blocks is pending before the Supreme Court, which referred it to mediation in October 2026. Nothing personal is pending.

proposal.counterweights: Reliance Industries reports spending ₹2,156 crore on corporate social responsibility in 2024-25, on rural development, education, healthcare and other programmes.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 1: level 3 needs a personal penalty or liability, and 'even if later dropped' covers indictments only. Both SEBI penalties naming Ambani were quashed and SEBI's appeals dismissed (Nov 2024), so none stands. What remains is a company regulatory breach upheld in 2026 after the fraud finding fell: level 1 (2 only if read as a major court finding). Unresolved 0 to 2: KG-D6 is a pending company case. Politics stays 2; the Qwik link is reported and disputed. Ecology stays 4. Social not scored.
